Psychic (Japanese: サイコキネシス Psychokinesis) is a damage-dealing Psychic-type move introduced in Generation I.

It is

  • TM29 from Generation I to Pokémon Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon, and in Pokémon Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl.
  • TM40 in Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee!.
  • TR11 in Pokémon Sword and Shield.
  • TM120 in Generation IX.

It can be upgraded to the special Z-Move Genesis Supernova by Mew holding Mewnium Z.

Effect

Generation I

Psychic does damage and has a 33.2% chance of lowering the target's Special by one stage.

Generation II onwards

Psychic now has a 10% chance of lowering the target's Special Defense by one stage.

Psychic can be used as the first move of a Pokémon Contest combination, causing Confusion, Future Sight, Kinesis, and Teleport to score double the normal appeal if used in the next turn. It can also be used to finish a combination, with the user gaining 1 bonus appeal point if Calm Mind, Confusion, or Kinesis was used in the previous turn.

In other games

Pokémon Mystery Dungeon series

In Red Rescue Team and Blue Rescue Team, and Explorers of Time and Darkness, Psychic is a move with 18 base power, 88% accuracy, and 10 PP. It damages an enemy in front of the user, and might lower their Special Defense Defense by one stage.

In Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Explorers of Sky, the base power is raised to 38.

Pokémon UNITE

In Pokémon UNITE, Psychic is Mr. Mime's and Gardevoir's first move.

Mr. Mime can obtain the move by reaching level 4 and upgrading Fake Out into it instead of Confusion. After a short delay, the user creates a pulse of energy that damages enemies around themself and any target affected by Guard Swap, with a smaller pulse around any created Barriers or Light Screens. A debuff is placed on enemies for 3s, reducing their Sp. Def. by 15% for each blast they are hit with. Enemies hit by more than 1 pulse are stunned. At level 11, the attack also briefly slows.

Gardevoir can obtain the move by reaching level 7 as Kirlia and upgrading Confusion into it instead of Moonblast. The user fires a blast, damaging enemies in an area on impact. The blast creates a lingering field that damages, slows, and reduces Special Defense. At level 13, the move's cooldown is reduced.

Trivia

  • Psychic is the only move that has the same English name as that of one of the 18 types.
  • From Generation VI to Pokémon Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl, Psychic used an upgraded version of its original sound effect from Generations I and II.
